bios.meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct: Marie Curie was born Maria Skłodowska on November 7, 1867, in Warsaw, Poland. She studied physics and mathematics at the Flying University, a secret institution for women, and later moved to Paris to pursue further education at the Sorbonne, where she earned her degree in physics in 1893. Curie went on to earn her doctorate in physics from the Sorbonne in 1903 and became a professor of general physics at the University of Paris in 1906. She was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903, along with her husband Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel, for their pioneering work on radioactivity, and again in 1911, this time alone, for her work on the isolation of pure radium.

bios.mistralai/ministral-8b-2512: Marie Curie (born **Maria Skłodowska**) was born on **November 7, 1867**, in **Warsaw, Poland** (then part of the Russian Empire). Curie died on **July 4, 1934**, in **Sallanches, France**, from **aplastic anemia**, likely caused by prolonged exposure to radioactive materials.
